channel.title: Lapland.blog · Field journal from Finnish Lapland
channel.description: A first-person field journal from Finnish Lapland: honest, seasonal, written by someone who actually lives here. Aurora, cabins, seasons, food, people.

item.title: Seven and a half minutes a day: how fast autumn daylight fades in Lapland
item.description: The further north you go, the faster autumn light drains away. In Utsjoki the day shrinks by more than ten minutes a day in November, until the sun stops rising altogether.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: 154 Finnish rest areas lose maintenance or firewood: the Lapland list
item.description: In Lapland, dozens of rest areas between Lemmenjoki and Savukoski lost their maintenance or their firewood in 2026. Next in line, from the start of 2027: Salla, Tuntsa, Pyhä-Luosto and Sodankylä.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Packing for Lapland in July: a checklist and the reasons behind it
item.description: July in Lapland calls for clothes for two kinds of weather: afternoons are often warm, nights are cool, and it rains about every other day.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Wood-fired sauna at a Lapland cabin: how to heat it, step by step
item.description: Close the damper on a wood-burning sauna stove only when there are no flames or glowing embers left. Carbon monoxide has no smell, and it's unlikely to wake anyone who is asleep.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Rovaniemi market square in summer: where it is and what is in season
item.description: Some sellers rent their pitch for the whole season and others come for a single day, so the stalls on the square can change from day to day.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Night hiking at Kiilopää in July: trails, light and safety
item.description: At Kiilopää the sun doesn't set at night until mid-July, and the nights stay light into early August. Five marked trails start right beside the fell centre.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Sodankylä's midnight sun: when it shines and how to sleep
item.description: In Sodankylä the sun stays in the sky for 44 days in a row, and from early May to early August the nights never get dark.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Polar night in Rovaniemi: how dark it really gets and what helps
item.description: In Rovaniemi the sun rises every day of the year: even on the shortest day it stays up for just over two hours. Polar night, when it doesn't rise at all, begins further north.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Salmon soup in Rovaniemi: where to get it and what it costs
item.description: Four restaurants in Rovaniemi have salmon soup on the menu. In November you can have it for lunch in the centre at Roka or Cafe & Bar 21, and from the end of the month at Nili too.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Winter cabin in Lapland: heating, water, power and what to pack
item.description: The same booking site lists cabins with electric heating and a shower, and cabins where water comes from a well and the lights run on solar power. Only the listing tells you which is which.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: How to read an aurora forecast: Kp, solar wind, Bz and clouds
item.description: Kp is an average for the whole planet, and none of the stations behind its live estimate is in Finland. In Lapland the aurora is common even when space weather is calm.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Northern lights in Kemi: where to watch, light pollution and sea ice
item.description: Kemi lies south of the usual auroral zone, so on a quiet night the aurora stays low in the north, and seen from the shore, that's where the town lights are.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)
